solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Revolutionary workers with poster by tree appear striking

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the workers' abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the UK body representing workers
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A militant trade unionist pins up a poster beside a tree and looks impressive doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns TUC into CUT. The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is the British federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom meaning to make a stylish, eye-catching impression.

clue.text: A couple of fellows supporting church? Rubbish

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit beneath the church abbreviation

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, so two of them are FF

explanation.surface: Two men hold up a church building, and someone dismisses the whole thing as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting' means sitting underneath, so the couple of fellows comes below the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is the husks separated from grain, hence worthless stuff or nonsense.

clue.text: A descent that's very flaky?

parts.note: a downhill rush made of flakes, read as snow pouring down a mountainside rather than an unreliable person

explanation.surface: Someone describes a decline or a person who is extremely unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaky' suggests unreliable or crumbly pastry, but here it means made of snowflakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountain is literally a descent of flakes.

clue.text: Foolish error following American in Spain

indicators.note: the error comes after the American abbreviation, so it is placed second

parts.note: a sin is a moral error or wrongdoing
taken as written
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A Yank abroad in Spain makes a silly mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid or silly, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Taxi transferring Kay reaching race

indicators.note: transferring suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Kay switches transport mid-race to reach the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferring' rearranges all fifteen letters of KAY REACHING RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney carriage is the formal British legal term for a licensed taxi cab.

clue.text: Boost man reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the man's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Philip is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told a man gave them encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or something that gives a lift.

clue.text: Praise excessively coffee in France

indicators.note: in puts the coffee inside the abbreviation for France

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A tourist gushes over a cup of coffee in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone is to compliment them insincerely or too much.

clue.text: Free time leads to lots enjoying idleness? Definitely

indicators.note: leads are the front letters, here of the next three words

parts.note: sure as an interjection means definitely, certainly

explanation.surface: Spare time means plenty of lazing about, says a confident speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes the initials of lots, enjoying and idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is time free from work or duties, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Quiet journalist in new influential legal decision

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: in places the journalist inside the word for new

parts.note: recent means new or lately happened
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A discreet reporter is involved in a fresh, important court ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier court ruling that binds or guides later judgments.

clue.text: A vacant look shown by boxer? It's not acid

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the first and last letters of look remain

parts.note: Muhammad Ali is the famous boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer gives a blank stare, and someone points out it isn't sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties look to LK. Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion, is the crossword's usual boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a base, the chemical opposite of an acid.

clue.text: College owns site for developing discipline

parts.note: to own is to have, so owns gives has

indicators.note: developing land reshapes it, so the letters of site are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college holds a plot of land for building on.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish or rebuke, and discipline as a verb means the same.

clue.text: Spot at Scottish island removing a feature that's obsessive?

parts.note: being in a fix means being in a spot of trouble
taken as written

indicators.note: removing signals that a letter is taken out of the island

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland
the letter a as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fixture on a Scottish island and frets about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing a' takes an A from IONA to leave ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is an obsession, a trait or characteristic that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Holding figure by river

parts.note: ten is a number, or figure
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A number is placed beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a North Yorkshire river much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenure is a holding, as in the period or right of holding land or office.

clue.text: Hear about game barring outsiders? There's deception

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the court word goes round the game

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

indicators.note: barring outsiders means the outer letters of the game are dropped

parts.note: cricket is a bat-and-ball game

explanation.surface: Listening in on a game with no outsiders allowed looks suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge's verb, not listening; 'barring outsiders' trims the game's first and last letters, and 'about' wraps the court word round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery is deception or the use of tricks to cheat.

clue.text: Very difficult assignment from diminutive monks? The opposite!

definitions.meaning: a demanding task that is hard to fulfil
small religious order inverted: a lofty group of monks

explanation.surface: A tough job set by a bunch of little monks, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes a group of monks as an order; the opposite of diminutive is tall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a request that is unreasonably hard to meet.

clue.text: Go back about top person in court, we hear

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, so its sound gives other spelling

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament, on court

explanation.surface: An official asks to return regarding a senior figure in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court and its seeded player.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw.

clue.text: View a Merc that's crashed — it keeps the police busy?

indicators.note: a crashed car is smashed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at a Mercedes that has been wrecked: the police are busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's crashed' rearranges VIEW A MERC. A Merc is a Mercedes car.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime wave is a sudden rise in offences, which keeps officers stretched.

clue.text: Something used to explain a digit?

definitions.text: Something used to explain a digit?

parts.words: Something used to explain a digit?
parts.note: a map key explains symbols; the digit is also a toe, found at the bottom of a limb

explanation.surface: A request for an explanation of a number.
explanation.walkthrough: A legend is a map key, and split as LEG END it describes where a toe sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the key explaining symbols on a map, and a toe is at the limb's end.

clue.text: Fine start to afternoon going round a Spanish city

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the fine word surrounds the letter

parts.note: grand means fine or splendid

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: A pleasant early afternoon is spent strolling around a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to afternoon' gives A, which 'going round' puts inside GRAND before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Lose strength having drunk odd wine

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flags after drinking some strange wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ODD WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To die down is to subside or weaken gradually.

clue.text: Satisfactory — and nothing left presumably?

definitions.meaning: if everything is to the right side, there is nothing on the left

explanation.surface: Things are fine, and there's nothing remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes left as the opposite of right, not remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: All right means acceptable, and read literally means everything on the right.

clue.text: Easygoing Helen I enticed? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of these words is used, the answer sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A relaxed Helen is only partly tempted.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and not strict, close to easygoing.

clue.text: Order, say, embodied by superior angel

indicators.note: embodied by means contained within, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: A command is given by a heavenly being of higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Order is one example of an order, a fraternal organisation.

clue.text: Untainted Northern railwaymen recalled second

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: pure means untainted
the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in the UK

explanation.surface: Clean-living railway workers from the north are brought back for another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns PURENNUR into the answer. The NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up comes second in a contest.

clue.text: Pasty extremely tasty? Goodness!

parts.note: a pasty is a kind of pie

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of tasty

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a pasty that's really delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasty is a British pastry case with savoury filling. 'extremely' gives TY from tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious goodness or devotion.

clue.text: A drop is spilt before a popular scattering?

indicators.note: before places the anagram ahead of the single letter
spilt means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter a as written

explanation.surface: A drop of liquid spills ahead of a widely liked dispersal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges A DROP IS into DIASPOR. Popular here means of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people from their homeland, a scattering of populace.

clue.text: Initially embarrassing mistake to pass

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of embarrassing

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: An awkward slip is let go by.
explanation.definitionFit: To elapse is for time to go by or pass.

clue.text: Crime time forgot? Motive needed

indicators.note: forgot means left out, so the time abbreviation is removed

parts.note: treason is the crime of betraying one's country

explanation.surface: A crime whose timing was forgotten still needs an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is a cause or motive behind an action.

clue.text: Request Eastern feast in US city

indicators.note: in places the feast inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
a treat is a delightful feast

explanation.surface: An eastern dinner held in an American city prompts an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.
